A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same procedural-pretraining study. The complete main texts, figures, tables, and Appendices A–N are readable and support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original training, transfer, ablation, scaling, and downstream fine-tuning experiments in Sections 4–6 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds MBPP code-generation and ARC-Easy/HellaSwag evaluation results.

M1.justification: The procedural generators, GPT-2-style models, training objectives, full/selective weight transfer, and data- and weight-mixture procedures are retained. The added downstream evaluations use the existing approach.

E1.justification: Section 5.3 adds MBPP code generation, while Appendix M.2 adds ARC-Easy and HellaSwag reasoning evaluations. These extend downstream task coverage within the existing language and code domains; the earlier training corpora, diagnostic tasks, and downstream datasets remain.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same no-procedural-pretraining baseline, transfer variants, shuffled controls, and mixture comparisons. The added benchmarks compare models with and without procedural pretraining; they introduce no additional comparator method.

E3.justification: v2 introduces three-shot MBPP evaluation using pass@k at k = 1, 5, 10, and 80, plus zero-shot accuracy evaluation on ARC-Easy and HellaSwag. These are protocols for added experiments; the retained experiments' stated training budgets, splits, and evaluation procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The attention-entropy, selective-head transfer, weight-shuffling, noise, sequence-length, pretraining-loss, vocabulary-size, and weight-decay analyses are retained. Their relocation and renumbering do not introduce new ablations or robustness tests.

E5.justification: Appendices E.2 and N retain the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting over 10 seeds, with three seeds for multiplication. The new downstream comparisons provide point estimates without introducing additional uncertainty estimation or repeated-run reporting.

E6.justification: The retained result tables match after renumbering. New Table 7 reports procedural versus baseline accuracy of 38.2% versus 37.3% on ARC-Easy and 28.3% versus 27.6% on HellaSwag. New Figure 7 shows positive MBPP success with procedural pretraining while the baseline remains at zero through 80 attempts.

T1.justification: The token-budget relations, mixture formulation, and attention-entropy equation are unchanged. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and v2 introduces no substantive mathematical derivation or assumption.

C1.justification: The four principal contributions remain. v2 broadens the downstream-utility claim to code generation and commonsense reasoning, and the abstract and introduction explicitly claim FLOP reductions comparable to the previously reported token savings.

C2.justification: Section 5.4 qualifies the earlier statement that MLP transfer is most effective for natural language to the narrower comparison that it is better than attention transfer, matching Figure 6 more accurately. Section 7 additionally acknowledges the experiments' lower data-to-model ratio as a limitation.

D1.justification: Appendix E.3 explicitly identifies the 124M models and clarifies training-recipe provenance. The code-access pointer changes from a repository to a project page, and the promise of a forthcoming documented release disappears. These are documentation changes; the PDFs do not establish a change in actual code availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bloem (2025), Jesus et al. (2021), and references for MBPP, ARC, and HellaSwag. The broader positioning and extended literature review remain stable. Dong's changed title and Shinnick's publication update refer to retained works.

P1.justification: v2 edits the abstract and introduction, clarifies terminology, promotes downstream evaluation to Section 5.3, and subdivides Appendix M. It also replaces the reproducibility statement with an impact statement. The overall narrative and most substantive prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The main text and references switch from single-column to two-column conference formatting, substantially changing figure/table sizing and placement. Figure 4 changes from side-by-side to stacked panels, Figure 2 gains best-performer labels, and v2 adds MBPP Figure 7 and commonsense Table 7. Appendix displays are extensively redistributed.

improvement.justification: Figure 7 and Table 7 extend practical validation beyond v1's downstream fine-tuning experiments. The more accurate MLP-transfer interpretation and added data-to-model-ratio limitation also improve precision. Limited setup and uncertainty reporting for the new evaluations constrain their evidential strength, so the overall quality gain is modest.
